newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Lamont to focus on improving profitability.
newsitem.headline: Lamont to focus on improving profitability.

text.p: Belfast-based textiles group Lamont Holdings Plc said on Wednesday that its principal focus in 1997 would be the delivery of performance improvement.
The company, which earlier reported a 1996 pre-tax loss of 8.64 million sterling against a profit of 9.7 million in 1995, said it had set clear improvement targets in each of its businesses.
For the first time in recent years, all its operations were trading profitably and Lamont said it was taking tangible action to improve profitability irrespective of the market environment.
It said the immediate prospects for the UK economy appeared promising but said this did not necessarily translate into strong demand for all its products and services.

"The strength of sterling has reduced competitiveness in certain key export markets and increased the attractiveness of certain products imported into the UK," Lamont said in its annual results statement.
The company attributed last year's overall loss to impact of trading losses at Shaw Carpets, a loss on its disposal and restructuring charges at Moygashel.
Turnover from continuing operations was down four percent at 99.2 million, mainly because of low turnover at Moygashel in the early part of the year.

Operating profits from Lamont's continuing operations were broadly unchanged at 9.4 million sterling against 9.6 million a year earlier while operating margins improved to 9.5 percent from 9.3 percent, the company said.

The disposal of Shaw, which took a disproportionate share of Lamont's resources and effort away from other group activities, should allow the company to focus on operations where it has already demonstrated competitive advantage, the company said.
Lamont said one of the most encouraging features of the results was the strength of cash generation from its continuing operations which exceeded 20 million sterling.
Along with the anticipated proceeds from the sale of Shaw Carpets, this should result in a considerable strengthening of the balance sheet, Lamont said.

Net debt was reduced to 21.0 million from 23.7 million last year, resulting in year-end gearing of 48 percent and gross cash proceeds of around seven million from the sale of Shaw and a warehouse should further cut gearing to less than 35 percent.

"This stronger balance sheet position, together with the actions taken at Moygashel and Shaw Carpets, enables management to concentrate on the delivery of increased profitability for the group," the company said.
Lamont maintained its full-year dividend at 12.8 pence per share.
